dedupe_keys.name: floris wake modelling and wind farm controls software

description: FLORIS is a controls-focused wind farm simulation package that places steady-state engineering wake models in a performance-focused Python framework. It has been developed since 2013 at the US national laboratory now called the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), mainly with support from the US Department of Energy, and is part of the Wind Energy Technologies Office software stack. Users build wind farms from layouts and turbine definitions, choose wake models, and compute turbine power and flow fields, with tools for controls such as yaw steering and for layout optimisation, some using pyOptSparse. The method is location-independent. It installs from PyPI for Python 3.10 to 3.14, with online documentation and GitHub Discussions, and version 4.6.6 is the latest release; version 3.6 was the last of the v3 line. It is licensed under BSD-3-Clause at no cost. Caveats: engineering wake models trade accuracy for speed, and upgrading from v3 to v4 needs a new environment. Simulation uses are wind farm control and layout optimisation and fast farm-level power estimates for grid studies. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
